clue.text: Return of one breaking up some land for heath

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the whole built piece is read from right to left
the numeral splits the land measure apart, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: an acre is a measured piece of land
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone ploughing up a plot of ground to make a heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' puts I inside ACRE to give ACIRE, and 'Return of' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heathers, so heath is its common name.

clue.text: Just a remnant, so it's useless to carry on here

definitions.text: Just a remnant, so it's useless to carry on here

parts.words: Just a remnant, so it's useless to carry on here
parts.note: a final scrap of something is reached at a point beyond which going further is pointless, like the last stop of a railway

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the final point where nothing more can be done, and also the terminus of a railway.

clue.text: Hidden, like some exports

definitions.meaning: out of sight, unable to be seen
services such as banking and tourism sold abroad are counted as exports that cannot be seen

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unseen, and in economics names exports of services rather than goods.

clue.text: Make up notice attracting a Liberal

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: A newspaper notice catches the eye of a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting a' is link material joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to improvise, to make up words on the spot.

clue.text: Sarah, when next to sink, more pallid

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
to sink something is to lower it

explanation.surface: Sarah looks paler when standing beside the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when next to' simply sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion, so the comparative means paler or more pallid.

clue.text: Trivial fling seen at the table

parts.note: small means minor or trivial
to slam something is to fling it down hard

explanation.surface: A minor affair is spotted at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is the card table: in bridge a small slam is winning twelve of thirteen tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: This bridge contract is something made at the card table, which the clue uses as its definition.

clue.text: Wrong turning for lodge

indicators.note: turning means reversing the order of the letters

parts.note: evil is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Taking a wrong turn on the way to a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to live or reside there.

clue.text: Carrots he chopped up as an accompaniment?

indicators.note: chopping reduces vegetables to pieces, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook prepares carrots as a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' signals rearranging CARROTS HE. The question mark warns that accompaniment is musical, not culinary.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra may accompany a soloist or singer, providing the musical accompaniment.

clue.text: Bit player gets former friend to go half way

parts.note: an ex is a former partner or friend

indicators.note: only half the way is covered, so the word keeps its first half

parts.note: to go somewhere is to travel

explanation.surface: A minor actor persuades an old flame to meet halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half way' keeps TRA, the first half of TRAVEL; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film or stage performer with a non-speaking bit part.

clue.text: Provocative debater makes David eat cloves

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd recipe in which David is forced to eat cloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a loose anagram signal here: DAVID EAT CLOVES has exactly the fourteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues the opposite case to provoke discussion is said to play this role, from the Church official who argued against canonisation.

clue.text: Champions new roasting pots

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Award-winning new cookware for roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals rearranging ROASTING POTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Protagonists are leading advocates of a cause, so champions of it.

clue.text: Dish remains hot and black in autumn

indicators.note: the remaining pieces sit within the season's name

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
as in 'the problem remains', so the verb is taken as IS
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A plate of leftovers, kept hot and burnt black, in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the other pieces inside the season's American name, after its first letter; 'remains' is read as the verb in 'the problem remains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishball is a rissole of minced fish, served as a dish.

clue.text: No longer go for fix

definitions.meaning: the verb once meant to go or betake oneself somewhere, as in 'they ... to the inn', a sense now dated

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to mend and, in an old-fashioned usage, to go to a place.

clue.text: Frightful apparition makes you warmer and go blind, nearly

parts.note: a hob is a cooking surface that warms pans
taken as written

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: unable to see

explanation.surface: A ghost so terrifying it makes you sweat and lose your sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the last letter from BLIND, leaving BLIN. 'makes you' is a link: the pieces make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous imp or bogey, a frightening apparition in folklore.

clue.text: Obsolete copper taken to bank in a haze

parts.note: obs is the dictionary abbreviation for obsolete
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: An outdated copper coin is carried to the bank in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Done obscurely means done unclearly, as if hidden in a haze.

clue.text: Sleep wear: dark, grand and personal

parts.note: night is the dark time of day
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
one's own things are personal to one

explanation.surface: Description of a dark, impressive and private item of bedwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn in bed, so sleepwear.

clue.text: I remain in dry part of Asia

indicators.note: the two pieces sit within the abbreviation for dry

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal, someone who stays off alcohol
to be is to exist or remain

explanation.surface: A traveller vows to stay in some arid region of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal, a British usage for someone who abstains from alcohol, and 'in' puts the other pieces inside its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan plateau region lies in central Asia, under Chinese rule.

clue.text: Newly-married woman gets strong in prison

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
well means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: A new wife gets tough while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridewell, named after a London jail, is an old word for a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name became a general term for a jail.

clue.text: The sound of guides in northern England

indicators.note: the word is what one hears when the clue word is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a person who guides others leads them

explanation.surface: The voice of a tour guide heard in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Yorkshire city lies in northern England; the clue defines it by its location.

clue.text: Going away with fancy rig in wedding

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the word for wedding

parts.note: mating is the joining of a pair, a wedding of animals

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Heading off on honeymoon in a dressy outfit after the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the three letters of 'rig', and 'in' places them after the first letter of the word for wedding; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrating birds are going away to another region for the season.

clue.text: Look back at subminiature cloud

indicators.note: looking back means reading in the reverse direction
the letters are found at, that is within, the following word

explanation.surface: An instruction to review a tiny photograph of a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBMIN sits at the start of 'subminiature'; 'Look back' reads it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain-bearing grey cloud, also a halo.

clue.text: Irish girl doctor, one going after the taxmen

indicators.note: the letter for one comes after the taxmen's abbreviation

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An Irish woman doctor chases the tax collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax office.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a girl's name of Irish origin, an anglicised form of Máire.

clue.text: A good person to advise on fish

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
to urge someone is to advise them strongly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Looking for an expert who can tell you about fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking an expert; 'to' is a link joining the saint and URGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, caviar.

clue.text: Religious teaching on the heavens is dangerous

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a British school subject
the sky is the vault of the heavens

explanation.surface: A lesson on the heavens proves hazardous for believers.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was a school subject in Britain; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky means involving danger or hazard.

clue.text: Scrap for a cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Leftovers saved to feed a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like food for a pet, but means a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest bit of something, a scrap.

clue.text: I use lion's scent, which might lead to promiscuity

indicators.note: the words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: here the S of the possessive counts as a letter

explanation.surface: A man wears a musky big-cat perfume hoping it will make him irresistible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might lead to' signals rearranging I USE LIONS SCENT, all fourteen letters including the S of lion's.
explanation.definitionFit: Licentiousness is lack of sexual restraint, much the same as promiscuity.

clue.text: Gladys loses head to Guy, who is courteous to women

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter of the name

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man

explanation.surface: Gladys is beheaded by a Guy who is gallant to ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' takes G off GLADYS, giving LADYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is one who enjoys the company of women and is attentive to them.

clue.text: Squeals "yes" when holding the record

indicators.note: the agreement word holds the record inside it

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Shrieks of delight when someone wins the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when holding' puts the record inside the agreeing word; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelps are short sharp cries, much like squeals.
